clue.text: Entranced over golden eagle

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting over another means it comes first

parts.note: someone entranced is rapt, wholly absorbed
or is the heraldic word for gold, so golden

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher is spellbound watching a golden eagle.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle is a bird of prey, and raptor is the general term for such hunting birds.

clue.text: A variety of gravel found in Portugal

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them, so the word gravel is shuffled

explanation.surface: A particular type of gravel turns up in Portugal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' gives LGARVE. The Algarve is Portugal's southern coastal region, popular with holidaymakers, so 'found in Portugal' fairly defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Algarve is the southernmost region of Portugal, a place found within that country.

clue.text: The woman all on her own from choice

definitions.text: The woman all on her own from choice

parts.words: The woman all on her own from choice
parts.note: describes a woman who has chosen a life of solitude, as a religious recluse walled away from the world does

explanation.definitionFit: A female religious recluse lived voluntarily shut away in a cell, alone by choice.

clue.text: Article framed by shrewd old king

indicators.note: something framed by another word sits inside it, so the article goes within the word for shrewd

parts.note: cute can mean clever or shrewd
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece is surrounded by remarks about a canny monarch of long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: Canute was an eleventh-century king of England, Denmark and Norway.

clue.text: A winger, a Greek character, gone berserk

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: berserk means wild and out of control, so the letters of the word gone are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wing player, some Greek fellow, has lost his temper on the field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone berserk' gives GEON. 'winger' suggests a footballer on the flank, but here it is any creature with wings.
explanation.definitionFit: A pigeon is a bird, a creature that flies on wings.

clue.text: Deplorable way to call for retirement

parts.note: a path is a way or track

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for call is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call or summon, as a witness

explanation.surface: Asking someone to retire seems a miserable way to do things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for retirement' gives ETIC; the surface suggests a sad send-off for a retiring worker, but retirement here just means going backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pathetic in the sense of feeble and contemptible matches deplorable, woefully bad.

clue.text: Edgar's rebellious girl

indicators.note: rebellious letters refuse to stay in order, so the name Edgar is rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Edgar has a daughter who will not behave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious' rearranges EDGAR; the 's is a possessive and gives no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerda is a female first name, as of the heroine of Andersen's The Snow Queen.

clue.text: Covered or left face-up?

explanation.definitionFit: Overlaid means coated with a layer; read as over and laid, it suggests something put down turned over, face up.

clue.text: Provided only of the same size

explanation.definitionFit: The conjunction means on condition that; read literally it compares two things of equal length.

clue.text: Shops keep one for the accounts

indicators.note: to keep is to hold within, so the word for shops holds the numeral

parts.note: stores are shops
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Retailers hold one copy for the bookkeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accounts' suggests bookkeeping, but here it means narratives or tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts in the sense of narrated reports or tales are stories.

clue.text: Give instruction to a pirate

explanation.definitionFit: To instruct someone is to school them; Edward Teach was the real name of the pirate Blackbeard.

clue.text: Fair to all — beer's ordered

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ordered letters have been put into a fresh sequence, so all and beer are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Drinks are bought for everyone, which seems only fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' gives LERABLE; the surface suggests buying a round of drinks, but the word is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair in the sense of middling, reasonably acceptable, is a synonym.

clue.text: No minister may appear eccentric

parts.note: no as nought, the figure zero, resembles the letter O
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a minister's qualification

explanation.surface: A church without a minister might seem rather strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Odd means strange or peculiar, much as an eccentric person is.

clue.text: Military personnel, proficient yet withdrawn

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
versed means skilled or knowledgeable

explanation.surface: Soldiers who are highly skilled have nevertheless pulled back.
explanation.definitionFit: A judgment withdrawn or revoked, as on appeal, has been overturned.

clue.text: Spoil a naughty child to show off

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
to air something is to display it

explanation.surface: A spoilt brat is ruined by parading him in public.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, much as spoiling does.

clue.text: Brought together about a hundred on drugs

indicators.note: the word for brought together goes about, around, the letter for a hundred

parts.note: to mediate is to bring opposing parties together
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Around a hundred people were assembled while under the influence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C into MEDIATED after its fourth letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicated means treated with medicine, so given drugs.

clue.text: Set out to entrap law-breaking firm

indicators.note: to entrap is to catch inside, so the word for set out holds the other letters

parts.note: to start is to set out on a journey

indicators.note: breaking the word law smashes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A plan is set in motion to catch a crooked company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' gives LWA, held by 'to entrap'. 'firm' looks like a company, which suits the crime story, but it is the adjective meaning steadfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart supporter is staunch, loyal and steadfast.

clue.text: Tell for instance

explanation.definitionFit: To tell is to speak or state; it also introduces an example, as e.g. does.

clue.text: A type of hormone that builds a heavenly body

parts.note: a steroid is one kind of hormone, like testosterone

explanation.surface: A hormone helps a bodybuilder develop a divine physique.
explanation.walkthrough: 'builds' and 'body' suggest bodybuilding and steroids, but 'heavenly body' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky object orbiting the sun, a celestial object.

clue.text: One's not entirely irreplaceable!

indicators.note: only part of the word irreplaceable is used, its letters taken from the middle

explanation.surface: A modest reminder that no one is wholly indispensable.
explanation.definitionFit: The ace is the card or die face counting as a single unit.

clue.text: A quarter lock emphasise that

parts.note: S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A hairdresser insists on fixing a quarter of a client's hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a point is to give it weight or prominence.

clue.text: An animal living in the sea perhaps

indicators.note: the answer lives inside the words sea perhaps, spanning them

explanation.surface: A creature that might dwell in the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An ape is a primate such as a gorilla or chimpanzee.

clue.text: The youngster presented to a princess

parts.note: an infant is a young child

explanation.surface: A baby is introduced to a royal daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese monarch.

clue.text: Invalids involved in pain test

indicators.note: involved means intricately twisted together, so pain and test are mixed up

explanation.surface: Sick people take part in a painful examination.
explanation.definitionFit: Invalids are sick people, those under medical care.

clue.text: A good-looker, a big shot in the underworld, holding on

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: one word holding another contains it, so the underworld god surrounds on

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god who rules the underworld
taken as written

explanation.surface: A handsome man who is a gang boss keeps going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big shot in the underworld' suggests a gangster, but it is Dis, the Roman god of the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth loved by Venus, so any very handsome man.

clue.text: Blunder in shamefaced to get a drink

indicators.note: the word for blunder goes in the word for shamefaced

parts.note: shy means bashful, embarrassed
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: An embarrassed person makes a mistake when ordering something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherry is a fortified wine from southern Spain.

clue.text: Paid attention after midnight, and looked bright

indicators.note: one word after another follows it, so the letter comes before the second word

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night is G
to listen is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone stayed alert late into the night and seemed sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is the letter in the middle of 'night', G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glistened means shone or sparkled, as wet surfaces do.

clue.text: Sense this would be a great deal

definitions.text: this would be a great deal

explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five senses; a sight also means a large amount, as in a sight better.

clue.text: Saying take little notice with advancing years

parts.note: an ad is a short advertisement, a small notice
age is the state of growing old

explanation.surface: We tend to pay less heed as we grow older.
explanation.definitionFit: An adage is a proverb or traditional maxim.

clue.text: Managed to continue making capital

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
to go on is to continue

explanation.surface: A firm was run steadily so as to make money.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangoon, now Yangon, was the capital city of Burma.

clue.text: Governor who's grim about rocky situation

parts.note: dire means dreadful or grim
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a tor is a rocky hilltop

explanation.surface: A ruler is pessimistic about a difficult predicament.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky peak, common on Dartmoor in south-west England; 'rocky situation' suggests trouble but means a rocky place.
explanation.definitionFit: A director serves on the governing board of a company or school.

clue.text: Tasted awful, so it's claimed

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of tasted are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone insists the food tasted terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Stated means declared or asserted, as a claim is.
